question: Gate B resolves a cited path and never opens the file. Measure the exposure and decide whether a content-anchored citation check is cheap enough to build.
why_it_matters: OPEN_ITEMS C15 plus B4's 'nothing resolves the anchor inside the file', and P18 then produced the instance: TheoriaLean.lean:148 cited for a line at :149, on the citation carrying that ruling's refusal.
ruling: do not build the content-anchor gate; close C15 as a recorded limitation. Adopt the range check, which has zero yield today and therefore cannot regress silently.

measurements.range_check_yield: 0 -- a range check catches nothing on this paper
measurements.miss_precision: hand-checked 2 of 12; both false reds (plan_stage.py:59 is correct and the paper elides it; gen_lean.py:722-724 is correct and the checker extracted junk instead of the real quote)

why_the_gate_fails: backtick pairing over markdown is unreliable -- double-backtick inline spans defeat a single-backtick regex; a correct version needs a CommonMark inline lexer
backticked filenames are citations rather than content (filtered; moved MISS from 14 to 12)
the paper legitimately elides inside quotations -- solve(..., prefer="stub") -- which no substring test handles and which is good writing, not a defect

deliverables.census.py: executable census of line-anchored citations; NOFILE / OUTOFRANGE / INRANGE
deliverables.anchor_content.py: the content-anchor probe that was measured and rejected

checked_in_passing: section 10.7's account of the SURVEY-*.md citations is accurate, not stale: the originals are untracked on an unpushed branch and the paper cites the committed byte-verbatim copies under runs/20260729T140000Z-P14-honesty-section/inputs-verbatim/, which is what the census resolved them to.
limitations: the census covers sections/ only; P18's own defect was in a runs/ artefact and nothing scans those
'all 22 INRANGE' is not 'all 22 correct' -- spot-checked, not proved
no independent adversary; subagent launches were dying on API 529 through the session, and the conclusion is a negative one, which is the direction a self-review is least trustworthy in
